# term-list.example.txt — the deterministic floor's term list (#65).
#
# COPY THIS FILE, DO NOT EDIT IT IN THE REPO.
#
#     mkdir -p ~/.config/orchestrator
#     cp scripts/orchestrator/term-list.example.txt ~/.config/orchestrator/term-list.txt
#     chmod 600 ~/.config/orchestrator/term-list.txt
#
# Then add the path to CTP_PII_PATHS in ~/.ctp-bridge.conf so the C1 guard stops
# Claude's tools reading it. The orchestrator reads it directly, not through a
# tool call, so the floor still works while Claude is blind to it.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
# One Org-sensitive term per line: codenames, internal hostnames, client names,
# project names. If a prompt contains one, the orchestrator forces `sensitive`
# and the cloud tier is removed from the eligible set — in EVERY mode, including
# CLAUDE-ONLY. You can be overruled by your own list; edit the list to proceed.
#
# WHY IT IS CODE AND NOT A PROMPT
# These terms are matched by code, with no model in the path. Putting them in the
# classifier prompt instead would leave them subject to the exact failure mode
# they exist to catch — a model that overlooks them or is argued past them.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE MOST SENSITIVE ARTIFACT ON THE BOX
# It is a distilled index of what you are protecting. Never commit it, never
# paste it into a chat, never ask Claude to review or improve it. It is a one-way
# door: once populated, iterate on it yourself or with the local model.
# Nothing that matches is ever named in a verdict, on stderr, or in the log.
#
# RULES
#   - one term per line; lines starting with # are comments; blanks ignored
#   - matching is case-insensitive and word-boundary (atlas does NOT match
#     atlassian), so terms do not fire inside unrelated words
#   - terms shorter than ORCH_TERM_MIN_LEN (default 3) are rejected at load with
#     a line number on stderr, and are not used for matching
#   - prefer distinctive terms. A short or common word over-matches, routes
#     everything local, and the pressure that follows is to switch the floor off
#
# The shipped file is deliberately EMPTY of terms. Anything here would be a
# generic guess, and a generic floor protects nothing.
